sentences.text:
Anil Kumar Agarwal S/O Shri Teekam Chand ... vs State Of
Rajasthan on 12 May, 2020

Author: Pankaj Bhandari
Bench: Pankaj Bhandari
 High Court Of Judicature For Rajasthan
 Bench At Jaipur
 S.B. Criminal Miscellaneous Bail Application No. 4644/2020
Anil Kumar Agarwal S/o Shri Teekam Chand Agrawal, R/o Kot Ka
Mohalla, Ward No. 6, Chaksu, P.s. Chaksu, Jaipur.

entities.text:
High Court Of Judicature For Rajasthan
 Bench At Jaipur
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
(At Present Accused Confined In Central Jail, Jaipur.)
 ----Petitioner  Versus State Of Rajasthan, through PP  ----Respondent For Petitioner(s) : Mr. Prahlad Sharma.
For State : Mr. Sher Singh Mahala, PP.
 HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE PANKAJ BHANDARI  Order 12/05/2020 1.
Heard counsel for the petitioner through video conferencing.
Learned Public Prosecutor is present in person in the Court.

2. Petitioner has filed this bail application under Section 439 of Cr.P.C.
3.

F.I.R. No.138/2020 was registered at Police Station Chaksu, District Jaipur for offence under Sections 270, 272, 273, 420, 467, 468, 471, 120-B of I.P.C.
4.
It is contended by counsel for the petitioner that at the most, offence under Sections 58 & 59 of Food Safety and Standard Act, 2006 is made out which is a bailable offence.
Conclusion of trial will take time.
5. Learned Public Prosecutor has opposed the bail application.
Anil Kumar Agarwal S/O
Shri Teekam Chand ... vs State Of Rajasthan

6. I have considered the contentions.
7. Considering the contentions put forth by counsel for the petitioner, I deem it proper to allow the bail application.

8. This bail application is accordingly allowed and it is directed that accused petitioner shall be released on bail provided he furnishes a personal bond in the sum of Rs.1,00,000/- (Rupees One Lac only).

Petitioner is further directed to submit two sureties in the sum of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty Thousand only) before the concerned Court within eight weeks after the withdrawal of the order of the lock-down.
9. If the aforesaid two sureties are not submitted within the aforesaid period, Court below would be free to initiate appropriate action against the petitioner.
10. However it is made clear that if the petitioner repeats the offence, State would be free to move application for cancellation of bail before the concerned Court.
(PANKAJ BHANDARI),J CHANDAN /17 Powered by TCPDF (www.tcpdf.org)
